questions.question: Paper strips are each cut into 4 equal parts, so one whole strip is 4 parts. In total, 11 of these equal parts are shaded, which is the fraction 11/4. Written as a mixed number, how much is shaded?
questions.explain: Divide 11 by 4: the quotient 2 tells how many whole strips, and the remainder 3 stays as 3 parts out of 4, so 11/4 = 2 3/4. The common trap is writing the remainder as the whole number and getting 3 2/4.

questions.question: Granola bars are each cut into 3 equal pieces, so one whole bar is 3 pieces. Nadia has 7 of these equal pieces, which is the fraction 7/3. Written as a mixed number, how many bars does she have?
questions.explain: Divide 7 by 3 to get quotient 2 remainder 1, so 7/3 = 2 1/3 — the quotient is the number of whole bars and the remainder is the leftover pieces. Swapping them gives the wrong answer 1 2/3.

questions.question: Oranges are each split into 5 equal segments, so one whole orange is 5 segments. A snack tray holds 17 of these equal segments, which is the fraction 17/5. Written as a mixed number, how many oranges are on the tray?
questions.explain: 17 divided by 5 is 3 with remainder 2, so there are 3 whole oranges and 2 segments left over: 17/5 = 3 2/5. Watch out for putting the remainder in front of the fraction, which gives 2 3/5.

questions.question: Waffles are each cut into 8 equal parts, so one whole waffle is 8 parts. On a plate there are 19 of these equal parts, which is the fraction 19/8. Written as a mixed number, how many waffles are on the plate?
questions.explain: 19 divided by 8 gives quotient 2 and remainder 3, so 19/8 = 2 3/8: 2 whole waffles plus 3 of the 8 parts. The usual mistake is trading the two numbers and writing 3 2/8.

questions.question: Change the improper fraction 23/6 into a mixed number.
questions.explain: Divide 23 by 6: 6 goes in 3 times (18) with 5 left over, so 23/6 = 3 5/6 and the leftover keeps the same denominator 6. Do not swap the quotient and remainder, which would give 5 3/6.

questions.question: Priya has 29/8 metres of ribbon for a science-fair display. Written as a mixed number, how many metres of ribbon does she have?
questions.explain: 29 divided by 8 is 3 remainder 5, so the ribbon is 3 whole metres plus 5/8 of a metre: 3 5/8 m. The remainder 5 must stay on top of the fraction, not become the whole number.

questions.question: Kai wants to write 25/7 as a mixed number. He divides 25 by 7 and gets a quotient of 3 with a remainder of 4. Which mixed number should he write?
questions.explain: The quotient counts the whole groups of 7 and the remainder is the leftover sevenths, so 25/7 = 3 4/7. Writing 4 3/7 means the quotient and remainder were swapped, and you can check it is wrong because 4 wholes would need 28 sevenths.

questions.question: At a Burnaby pizza party each pizza is cut into 7 equal slices. The class ate 45 slices in total, which is 45/7 pizzas. Written as a mixed number, how many pizzas did the class eat?
questions.explain: 45 divided by 7 is 6 remainder 3, so 6 whole pizzas were finished and 3 slices of a seventh pizza were eaten: 6 3/7. Writing 3 6/7 mixes up the number of whole pizzas with the leftover slices.

questions.question: Jordan is converting 19/5 to a mixed number. He divides 19 by 5, gets a quotient of 3 and a remainder of 4, and writes 4 3/5. Which mixed number is actually correct for 19/5?
questions.explain: The quotient 3 is how many whole groups of 5 fit inside 19, and the remainder 4 is the leftover fifths, so 19/5 = 3 4/5. Jordan swapped them; a quick check is that 4 wholes would already need 20 fifths, which is more than 19.

questions.question: Ella cuts 3 pieces of ribbon for an art project, and each piece is 7/4 metres long. Written as a mixed number, how many metres of ribbon does she use in total?
questions.explain: First add the quarters: 3 pieces of 7/4 make 21/4 metres. Then divide 21 by 4 to get 5 remainder 1, so the total is 5 1/4 m — the remainder 1 stays over the denominator 4 instead of becoming the whole number.

questions.question: At a picnic in Stanley Park, each of 5 friends drinks 7/8 of a litre of juice. Written as a mixed number, how many litres of juice do they drink altogether?
questions.explain: Five lots of 7/8 make 35/8 litres, and 35 divided by 8 is 4 remainder 3, so they drink 4 3/8 L. The trap is writing 3 4/8, which puts the leftover eighths in the whole-number spot.

questions.question: Three cyclists on a Kelowna trail rode 5 km, 6 km and 8 km. The mean distance is 19/3 km. Written as a mixed number, what is the mean distance?
questions.explain: The mean is 19 divided by 3, which is 6 with a remainder of 1, so the mean is 6 1/3 km. The remainder 1 becomes 1/3 of a kilometre, not the whole-number part — 1 6/3 comes from swapping the quotient and remainder.
